label: late original-phase / <DEL> steps of letter-only sequences starting n/o/r with an early a (specific token conjunction)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.01% of steps, ~1.1k sequences). It fires only at steps t=3..7 of the original phase or at the <DEL> step (41% of mass), and never in the copy phase. It appears to need a conjunction of token identities. The first token is usually n, o or r (lift 6-10x); a is usually at position 1 or 2, and m or l often at position 2-3; the previous input is often q, w, b, k or e; and there are no digits (76% of mass falls in digit-free sequences). Activations are strongest when all these cues co-occur, e.g. o r a a k w <DEL> and n a a q w w <DEL>. The cues seem to add up as a soft score rather than forming a clean rule. Every hard-rule predicate tried reached low precision (best dev F1 0.21, precision 0.15, mass recall 0.39), because most sequences matching the cues stay silent. No simple coherent description was found.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+4.54), orig0=o (+3.84), orig1=a (+3.80), orig0=r (+3.73), prev_tok=q (+3.45), prev_tok=w (+3.34). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.88), phase=2 (-4.46), prev3_tok=- (-2.45), in_count=1 (-0.48).
